summary: Corporate raider Frank Lorenzo bought up struggling US airlines from 1972, broke their unions through lockouts, scab labor and a Chapter 11 filing used to void contracts, and helped create today's tiered, cut-rate air travel.

evidence.note: born in New York City in 1940
elected president and CEO of Texas International in 1972
1974 ground workers strike at TI; four-month shutdown until the union folds
caught double voting in a rigged Columbia student election
Continental CEO Feldman's suicide after the employee buyout collapses
plan to file Chapter 11 to void union contracts at Continental
1983 strike turns violent: pipe bombs, police leaking striker data
company-loaned stock deal pays him far more than his cut salary
free-flight favours to an Australian governor; bankruptcy judge joins his law firm
takeover of Eastern and its abusive treatment of unionized staff
1989 Eastern machinists strike, sympathy strikes, collapse of his empire
forced out of airlines; later bid for a new carrier refused
